timeout-kill-is-a-group-kill: When a `reg add` outlives the 15 s deadline the TS calls `child.kill('SIGKILL')` on the one child handle onSpawn gave it, and the golden records that as a `kill` line in calls.json with signal SIGKILL and the pid. The Rust side may not hand-roll a kill (the Rust shutdown contract): it kills the helper's process group through gamelib_proc::kill_tree::terminate_group, so the replay asserts that the helper registered for this `reg add` was killed, and the warning line, but not the signal name. The warning text (`timed out after 15000 ms; killed reg add (pid <pid>)`) is compared up to the pid, which is a real process id in Rust. Cases: knownFixesRegistry--applyregistryfixes-skip-and-kill-sigkills-the-captured-child-on-timeout-and-warns-killed, bridge-timeout-kills-the-reg-add.
undefined-raw-input: A step whose TS input was `undefined` (a dllOverrides value, a missing exe) has the key absent in cases.json, because JSON has no undefined. The replay maps an absent key to the same `None` the TS saw, and the golden records `raw: null` for an absent raw input.
error-text: A rejection is recorded as the TS prints it (`threw: Error: boom`, `threw: Error: nope`). The Rust replay's run seam fails with the same message and the module formats `Error: <message>`, so the line is compared byte for byte; a Rust-originated spawn error would print differently and is not a recorded case.
spawn-env-is-the-whole-environment: spawns.json holds the whole environment the `reg add` was given as `env` (the tracer's base was empty), recorded over the pinned base: the fake HOME's eight variables plus PATH, LANG and USER, then the keys setupEnvVars and setupWineEnvVars add. The Rust replay builds the same pinned base and compares the map as a whole, with no key gained or lost.
calls-json-shape: calls.json lists `runWineCommand` (what the run seam handed the command runner: command parts, wait, protonVerb, skipPrefixCheckIKnowWhatImDoing, whether onSpawn was passed), `runner.run` (what the command runner handed the process runner) and `kill`, in call order. A launcher-path case is the only one with `runner.run` lines.
